originalSourceObject.name: Battle Ready

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: Don or doff an actual suit of armor in half its normal time, preserving its real steps, access, hands, closures and fit. NEW: apply this factor once to the selected suit's existing armor duration; do not automatically include shields, weapons, jewelry or other gear. Combine the separately authorized single helper's doff-time halving multiplicatively with this feat because they represent distinct sources, then round elapsed time upward once to a whole second. In initiative, spend enough complete Actions/turn intervals to cover that elapsed work without compressing an Action below its legal availability; partial progress is retained only to the extent the armor procedure actually permits. Extra helpers do not further halve the time. Interruption leaves the real partially completed state and does not make the armor usable sooner. Gain advantage on each actual initiative roll; this creates neither a new roll after order is established nor an extra turn. Multiple initiative-advantage sources do not stack.

originalSourceObject.name: Berserker
originalSourceObject.description: You can enter a battle rage.
originalSourceObject.effect: Once per long rest, you can rage for 1 minute, gaining +2 damage on melee attacks and resistance to physical damage.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: NEW: as a Bonus Action, spend the feat's one long-rest use to enter this feat rage for one elapsed minute. Gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, whether magical or nonmagical, and add 2 damage on each actual successful melee attack you own. The melee scope includes weapon, unarmed, natural and melee spell attacks; it is not limited to weapons. Add the flat 2 once to the attack's primary damage type before target defenses; it is not doubled by a critical hit and is not a separate hit, copied damage or spellcasting trigger. NEW: the rage ends early if you voluntarily end it as a Bonus Action or become Incapacitated. It does not require attacking or taking damage to continue, prohibit spellcasting/concentration, extend through repeated attacks, or grant unstated class rage features. Another real rage may coexist under its own rules, but same-scope resistance does not stack and bonuses obey their actual families; this feat's flat rider cannot be counted twice under aliases. A completed rest restores the use, not an encounter declaration.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: NEW full healing procedure: as an Action, spend one real healer's-kit charge to treat one adjacent legally reachable living creature. Choose ordinary stabilization only, or this feat's healing treatment. A full actual kit has ten charges, costs 5 gp and weighs 3 lb under the reviewed item rule; transfer or partial use never refills it. Healing treatment has one entitlement per recipient per that recipient's completed short or long rest, shared across all Healer practitioners. Commit that entitlement and the charge before resolution even if healing is later blocked. If the recipient is dying, first cause an actual dying-to-Stable transition using this paid kit use, then resolve ordinary healing of 2d4 plus the practitioner's signed Wisdom modifier, minimum zero before the normal healing pipeline. One charge funds both parts of this single treatment. If HP gain is blocked, the stabilization remains with its genuine recovery deadline; if positive HP returns, close that obsolete deadline normally. A recipient whose healing entitlement is spent may still receive ordinary kit stabilization for its real charge and Action, without more feat HP. Already Stable creatures can receive the once-per-rest healing but create no new stabilization trigger. This removes no Wounds, Injury, disease or death. Independently owned Field Medic/Field Surgeon triggers require their actual source/event and own limits, with no duplicated kit charge or invented second stabilization.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: Require Constitution 15 and actually owned Necrotic Affinity or Dark Fortitude, using their exact feat IDs. Gain resistance to necrotic and poison damage. NEW delayed-recovery procedure: once per completed long rest, after an actual positive-to-zero damage/loss event finishes its Core Instant Death, Wound and death processing and leaves you living at zero, you may commit the use to that real dying/Stable episode. Record a recovery deadline at the start of your next original regular turn, preserving its virtual marker if initiative changes. At that deadline, before the normal death save, if you are still living at zero in that same episode, attempt direct state recovery to 1 HP. Broad HP-gain prohibition blocks the point; it does not create stability or refund the use. Earlier positive healing closes the pending episode and cancels this later recovery without reducing HP; actual death cancels it and cannot be reversed. On actual successful recovery, NEW: gain a one-elapsed-minute rider adding 2 necrotic damage once to each genuine personally owned damaging attack/spell/feature event, before target defenses. Apply it once to a shared area roll/event, with each target resolving its own defenses; a mixed-type packet does not gain it per component. Fixed damage and actual ongoing source ticks can qualify, but copied/reflected damage, another creature's actions and newly invented split packets do not. The flat +2 is not doubled by critical hits. It is this feat's damage component, not ordinary spell damage for Lifeleech, and creates no new spell, hit, payment, resource event or damage root; it cannot recursively trigger itself. Direct recovery does not remove Wounds, Prone or an independent cause of Unconsciousness. It ends on its deadline or your actual death and does not stack with itself. Missing this delayed recovery or being killed before it never becomes a later corpse wake-up.
